content.value_statement: Complex AI tasks can exceed one agent context or mix incompatible responsibilities. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan coordinated agent systems with clear roles and controls.
actual_capabilities: Explains supervisor, swarm, and hierarchical agent architectures.
Guides task decomposition across specialized agent roles.
Describes context isolation strategies for complex workflows.
Provides coordination patterns for handoffs, voting, and debate.
Covers failure controls such as validation, retries, and circuit breakers.
Includes framework-oriented examples for LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI.
limitations: It provides architecture guidance, not a complete production framework.
Example code needs adaptation before use in deployed systems.
It does not evaluate model costs or latency for a specific provider.
It does not replace security review for tools assigned to agents.

use_cases.title: Plan a Research Agent Team
use_cases.description: Design researchers, analysts, fact checkers, and writers with clear handoffs and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Single Agent Workflow
use_cases.description: Split a crowded agent prompt into focused workers that preserve context and reduce coordination noise.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Failure Modes
use_cases.description: Identify bottlenecks, divergence risks, consensus errors, and retry boundaries before production rollout.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need a multi-agent design for this task: [task]. Recommend supervisor, swarm, or hierarchy. Explain the main tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Define Agent Roles
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate decomposition of a complex task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this workflow into specialized agents: [workflow]. For each agent, define inputs, outputs, tools, and handoff rules.

prompt_templates.title: Add Coordination Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent architecture: [architecture]. Add validation, consensus, retry, timeout, and circuit breaker controls.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this multi-agent system for context isolation, token cost, latency, failure propagation, and observability. Provide concrete design changes.

output_examples.input: A team needs an agent system for long-form market research and report writing.
output_examples.output: A supervisor pattern with researcher, analyst, fact checker, and writer agents. The supervisor validates outputs and forwards final sections without rewriting details.

output_examples.input: A support workflow must route billing, technical, and sales questions to different specialists.
output_examples.output: A handoff design with a triage agent, three specialist agents, shared state, and confirmation messages after each transfer.

output_examples.input: An existing agent loop fails when one worker repeats errors.
output_examples.output: A failure plan with retry limits, cooldown windows, alternate workers, output validation, and alerts for repeated task failures.

best_practices: Use separate agents only when context isolation or specialization improves the outcome.
Define handoff contracts before adding more agents to the workflow.
Validate each agent output before another agent depends on it.
anti_patterns: Creating many role names without clear task boundaries or shared state rules.
Letting a supervisor rewrite specialist outputs when exact details matter.
Using simple majority voting when agents have unequal expertise or confidence.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when one agent has too much context, too many tools, or too many distinct responsibilities.

faq.question: Does this skill build agent software automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance, examples, and review prompts for building agent systems.

faq.question: Which architecture pattern is simplest to start with?
faq.answer: The supervisor pattern is usually simplest because one coordinator owns routing, validation, and final synthesis.

faq.question: How does it help with context limits?
faq.answer: It shows how to split work so each agent keeps only the context needed for its subtask.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that coordinate specialized agents.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review tool permissions, data sharing, output validation, latency, token cost, and failure recovery behavior.
